issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award cannot be set aside merely because the arbitrator allegedly reached a wrong conclusion, failed to appreciate facts, or acted contrary to a statutory obligation where those objections fall outside the limited grounds for challenge.
material_facts: The parties appeared before an umpire appointed by the Court, who made a reasoned award after lengthy proceedings.

An application was made to set aside the award in whole or in part, including on the grounds that the arbitrator had reached a wrong conclusion, failed to appreciate facts, and acted contrary to Section 70 of the Contract Act.
The Court found that the objections fell outside the limited grounds of challenge available under the Arbitration Act.
issues.conclusion: The objections were rejected and the award was directed to be made a rule of the Court.
issues.legal_principle: Under the scheme of the Arbitration Act, the arbitrator is the final arbiter of the dispute, and an award is not open to challenge merely because the arbitrator reached a wrong conclusion or failed to appreciate facts. An objection that the arbitrator acted contrary to Section 70 of the Contract Act is not a permissible ground for challenge on the facts of this case. The Court considered the appellant's reliance on Yogambai Boyee Ammani Animal v. Naina Pillai Markayar, ILR 33 Madras 15, but did not accept that reliance as permitting the challenge.

predicates.proceeding_seeks_to_set_aside_arbitral_a: A party applied to have an arbitral award set aside in whole or in part.
predicates.award_is_reasoned: The arbitrator issued an award that gave reasons.
predicates.objections_attack_merits_conclusions: The challenging party objected that the arbitrator reached a wrong conclusion or failed to appreciate the facts.
predicates.objection_alleges_conflict_with_restitut: The challenging party alleged that the arbitrator acted contrary to an obligation to make restitution for a benefit received.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to set aside a reasoned arbitral award on the basis of alleged errors in the arbitrator’s conclusions or fact assessment, or an alleged conflict with a restitution obligation, the objection is rejected and the award is upheld.
